fullPassage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her (A)[expectations / disappointments] about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so (B)[close / distant]. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were (C)[ruined / saved]. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 유럽 배낭여행에 대한 그녀의 기대는 정말 높았다. 그 경험들이 마침내 너무나 가까이 느껴졌다. 그녀의 계획은 망가졌다.
det.analysis:
① disappointments(실망)는 expectations의 반의어
② distant(먼)는 close의 반의어
③ expectations — close — ruined: 원문 그대로 ←정답
④ saved(구원된)는 ruined의 반의어
det.tip: expectations↔disappointments, close↔distant, ruined↔saved

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking (A)[forward / backward] to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she (B)[approached / avoided] the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to (C)[delay / advance] her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 1년 동안 그 여행을 고대해 왔다. 그녀가 카운터에 다가갔을 때, 직원이 여권을 보여달라고 했다. 꿈의 여행을 미뤄야 했다.
det.analysis:
① backward(뒤로)는 forward의 반의어
② forward — approached — delay: 원문 그대로 ←정답
③ avoided(피하다)는 approached의 반의어
④ advance(앞당기다)는 delay의 반의어
det.tip: look forward to↔look backward, approached↔avoided, delay↔advance

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She (A)[realized / overlooked] she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was (B)[heartbroken / delighted], knowing she could not (C)[board / exit] the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 여권을 집에 두고 왔다는 것을 깨달았다. 그녀는 비행기에 탑승하지 못한다는 것을 알고 가슴이 찢어졌다. 비행기에 탑승할 수 없었다.
det.analysis:
① realized — heartbroken — board: 원문 그대로 ←정답
② overlooked(간과하다)는 realized의 반의어
③ delighted(기뻐하는)는 heartbroken의 반의어
④ exit(나가다)는 board의 반의어
det.tip: realized↔overlooked, heartbroken↔delighted, board↔exit

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her ①<u>expectations</u> about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been ②<u>looking backward</u> to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she ③<u>approached</u> the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ④<u>ruined</u>. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ①기대 ②뒤를 돌아보다(→looking forward 고대하다) ③다가가다 ④망가진
det.analysis:
① expectations(기대): 원문 그대로
② looking backward(뒤를 돌아보다): looking forward(고대하다)의 반의어로 교체됨 — 여행을 1년간 '뒤돌아보다'는 문맥에 모순 ←정답
③ approached(다가가다): 원문 그대로
④ ruined(망가진): 원문 그대로
det.tip: looking forward↔looking backward. look forward to = ~을 고대하다

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to ①<u>visit</u> museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so ②<u>close</u>. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya ③<u>reached</u> into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was ④<u>overjoyed</u>, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ①방문하다 ②가까운 ③(손을) 뻗다 ④기쁨에 넘치는(→heartbroken 가슴이 찢어지는)
det.analysis:
① visit(방문하다): 원문 그대로
② close(가까운): 원문 그대로
③ reached(손을 뻗다): 원문 그대로
④ overjoyed(기쁨에 넘치는): heartbroken(가슴이 찢어지는)의 반의어로 교체됨 — 여권을 잃고 비행기를 못 타는데 '기쁨에 넘치는'은 문맥에 모순 ←정답
det.tip: heartbroken↔overjoyed. 여권 분실 상황에서 heartbroken이 자연스러움

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really ①<u>high</u>. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline ②<u>employee</u> asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to ③<u>hasten</u> her ④<u>dream</u> trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ①높은 ②직원 ③서두르다(→delay 미루다) ④꿈의
det.analysis:
① high(높은): 원문 그대로
② employee(직원): 원문 그대로
③ hasten(서두르다): delay(미루다)의 반의어로 교체됨 — 비행기 탑승이 불가한데 여행을 '서두르다'는 문맥에 모순 ←정답
④ dream(꿈의): 원문 그대로
det.tip: delay↔hasten. 여권 없이 탑승 불가 → 여행을 미뤄야(delay) 하는 상황

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she __________ the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그녀가 카운터에 __________했을 때, 항공사 직원이 여권을 보여달라고 요청했다.
det.analysis:
① approached(다가가다): 카운터에 다가가니 직원이 여권을 요청함 ←정답
② reached(손을 뻗다): 본문에 등장하나 reached는 '~에 손을 뻗다'의 의미로 카운터에 다가가다와 부적절
③ avoided(피하다): 카운터를 피하면 직원과 대화 불가
④ left(떠나다/두고 오다): 본문에 등장하나 카운터를 떠나는 것은 순서에 맞지 않음
det.tip: approach = 다가가다. 줄을 서서 기다리다 → 카운터에 다가가다

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She __________ she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 여권을 집에 두고 왔다는 것을 __________.
det.analysis:
① felt(느꼈다): 본문에 등장하나 '여권을 두고 왔다는 것을 느꼈다'는 부자연스러움
② denied(부인했다): 주머니에 아무것도 없는 상황에서 부인할 수 없음
③ waited(기다렸다): 본문에 등장하나 '여권을 두고 왔다는 것을 기다렸다'는 비문
④ realized(깨달았다): 주머니가 비어있음을 느끼고 깨달음 ←정답
det.tip: realize = 깨닫다. felt nothing → realized (연쇄적 인과관계)

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not __________ the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 비행기에 __________할 수 없다는 것을 알고 가슴이 찢어졌다.
det.analysis:
① visit(방문하다): 본문에 등장하나 '비행기를 방문하다'는 부적절
② board(탑승하다): 여권 없이 비행기에 탑승할 수 없음 ←정답
③ delay(미루다): 본문에 등장하나 '비행기를 미루다'는 주어가 맞지 않음
④ check(확인하다): 본문에 등장하나 문맥상 '비행기를 확인할 수 없다'는 부자연스러움
det.tip: board = 탑승하다. board the flight = 비행기에 탑승하다

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her <u>expectations</u> about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>expectations</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 유럽 배낭여행에 대한 그녀의 기대는 정말 높았다.
det.analysis:
① fears(두려움): 반의어에 가까움
② hopes(희망/기대): expectations의 동의어 ←정답
③ regrets(후회): 의미 무관
④ complaints(불평): 의미 무관
det.tip: expectations = hopes = anticipations

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she <u>approached</u> the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>approached</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그녀가 카운터에 다가갔을 때
det.analysis:
① departed(출발하다): 반의어
② abandoned(버리다): 의미 무관
③ neared(가까이 가다): approached의 동의어 ←정답
④ avoided(피하다): 반의어
det.tip: approached = neared = came close to

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were <u>ruined</u>. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>ruined</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그녀의 계획은 망가졌다.
det.analysis:
① fulfilled(이행된): 반의어
② improved(개선된): 반의어에 가까움
③ maintained(유지된): 반의어에 가까움
④ destroyed(파괴된): ruined의 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: ruined = destroyed = wrecked = devastated

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was <u>heartbroken</u>, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>heartbroken</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 가슴이 찢어지는 심정이었다.
det.analysis:
① thrilled(매우 기뻐하는): heartbroken(가슴이 찢어지는)의 반의어 ←정답
② sorrowful(슬픈): 동의어
③ devastated(망연자실한): 동의어
④ miserable(비참한): 동의어
det.tip: heartbroken(가슴이 찢어지는) ↔ thrilled(매우 기뻐하는)

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to check in for her flight. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to <u>delay</u> her dream trip.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>delay</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 꿈의 여행을 미뤄야 했다.
det.analysis:
① postpone(연기하다): 동의어
② suspend(중단하다): 유사어
③ expedite(촉진하다/서두르다): delay(미루다)의 반의어 ←정답
④ defer(미루다): 동의어
det.tip: delay(미루다) ↔ expedite(촉진하다/서두르다)

questions.passage:
(A) Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She <u>left</u> her passport at home.
(B) After the meeting, only three people <u>left</u> the room. The rest stayed behind to discuss the matter further.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 left가 (A)와 (B)에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 그녀는 여권을 집에 두고 왔다. (B) 회의가 끝난 후 세 사람만 방을 떠났다.
det.analysis:
① (A)와 (B) 의미 뒤바뀜
② (A) 남기다는 부정확, (B) 남기다도 부정확
③ (A) 떠나다는 부정확
④ (A) 두고 오다 — (B) 떠나다: 정확 ←정답
det.tip: left: ① 두고 오다/남기다 (leave sth behind) ② 떠나다 (depart from)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a journey or excursion, especially for pleasure"

det.korean: 특히 즐거움을 위한 여정이나 여행
det.analysis:
① flight(비행/비행편): 이동 수단이지 여행 전체 아님
② passport(여권): 여행 서류이지 여행 자체 아님
③ trip(여행): 영영풀이와 정확히 일치 ←정답
④ counter(카운터): 장소이지 여행 아님
det.tip: trip = a journey or excursion. 본문의 backpacking trip

questions.passage: Her __________ (expect) about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로) (1단어)

det.korean: 유럽 배낭여행에 대한 그녀의 __________은 정말 높았다.
det.analysis: expectations: expect(기대하다, 동사) → expectations(기대, 명사). Her _____ were high 구조에서 주어 역할 명사 필요, 복수형
det.tip: expect(동사) → expectation(명사) → expectations(복수)

questions.passage: She was heartbroken, __________ (know) she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로) (1단어)

det.korean: 그녀는 비행기에 탑승할 수 없고 꿈의 여행을 미뤄야 한다는 것을 __________며 가슴이 찢어졌다.
det.analysis: knowing: know(알다, 동사) → knowing(분사구문). 주절 She was heartbroken 뒤 분사구문 형태로 이유를 설명
det.tip: know → knowing (분사구문: ~하면서/~이므로). She was heartbroken, knowing ~

questions.passage: Maya waited in line to __________. Her expectations about her European backpacking trip were really high. She had been looking forward to the trip for a year. She couldn't wait to visit museums in Madrid and see the Eiffel Tower at night in Paris. As she stood in line, she could feel those experiences were finally so close. When she approached the counter, the airline employee asked to see her passport. Maya reached into her pocket and felt nothing. She realized she had left her passport at home. Her plans were ruined. She was heartbroken, knowing she could not board the flight and had to delay her dream trip.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Maya는 __________하기 위해 줄을 서서 기다렸다.
det.analysis:
① visit museums in Madrid: 본문 표현이지만 줄을 선 직접적 목적 아님
② check in for her flight: 줄을 선 목적은 비행기 체크인 ←정답
③ delay her dream trip: 여행을 미루려고 줄을 선 것이 아님
